A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 26-page versions of the same Speak Easy paper. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v2 reports original human evaluations, response-selection experiments, jailbreak benchmark results, and ablations in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including human judgments, benchmark scores, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The Speak Easy decomposition, translation, response selection, concatenation, and model-training procedures remain unchanged. The HarmScore correction concerns the evaluation metric and does not document a changed attack procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same preference-training datasets, human-evaluation data, language coverage, and four jailbreak benchmarks: HarmBench, AdvBench, SORRY-Bench, and MedSafetyBench.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including DR, GCG-T, TAP-T, and the appendix's Past Tense comparisons. Table 2 retains the same response-selection model baselines.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the stated HarmScore refusal gate from R ∩ S ≠ ∅ to R ∩ S = ∅. This revises the written evaluation metric; other protocols remain unchanged, and neither recomputation nor rerunning experiments is reported.

E4.justification: Sections 5.4–5.5 and Appendix C retain identical analyses of decomposition steps, language counts, response-selection strategies, refusal rates, and language contributions.

E5.justification: Statistical procedures and reporting are unchanged, including chi-square tests, Fleiss' kappa, Lasso regression, correlations, and annotation counts. No seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty information is added.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–4 and 10–12 and Figures 4–5 and 11. The formula correction is not accompanied by revised scores.

T1.justification: The HarmScore definition in Section 3.2 replaces the nonempty-intersection condition with an empty-intersection condition. This logical correction makes the equation score non-refusing responses, matching the existing prose. The remaining mathematics is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying actionability and informativeness, introducing HarmScore, and demonstrating harmful responses through simple multilingual, multi-step interactions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain unchanged, including HarmScore's difficulties with content-generation queries, diminishing gains from additional languages, and explanations of language-selection patterns.

D1.justification: Implementation prompts, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, decoding settings, and code-access information remain unchanged, including the details in Appendix B.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to existing jailbreak and evaluation approaches are identical.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 16 June 2025 to v3 dated 2 August 2025. Body prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and 12 tables retain the same designs, captions, and placement. Rendered comparisons establish unchanged page layout; the changed stamp text and equation symbol do not introduce a layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes the inverted refusal condition in HarmScore's formal definition, bringing it into agreement with the explanation already present in Section 3.2. This removes a misleading mathematical inconsistency. Experiments, results, and appendices remain unchanged, so the supported quality gain is limited to the metric's correctness and clarity.
